question.text: Celtic culture spread as far as this country after the ancient Galatians settled down. This country warred with Greece after World War I under its leader, Mustafa Kemal Ataturk.
question.clue: This country's penal code includes a controversial Article 301 that has been used to crack down on dissidents who have discussed the Armenian Genocide orchestrated by this country.

swap.text: After establishing the government of Ankara, this man led the War of Turkish Independence and became the first president of the Republic of Turkey.
swap.clue: He captured Mus while defeating Russian forces in the Caucasus, and this leader won the battle of Sakarya over the Greeks, earning the Treaty of Lausanne, which annulled the earlier and harsher Treaty of Sevres.

question.leadin: This emperor was the son of Selim the Grim.
question.text: Name this greatest of the Ottoman Emperors who conquered Hungary at the Battle of Mohacs in 1526 and besieged Vienna in 1529.
question.answerHtml: Suleiman the Magnificent [accept Suleiman the Lawgiver; accept Suleiman I; prompt on Suleiman]
question.clue: At the Battle of Mohacs, this ruler's forces killed Louis II, after which this ruler threw his support behind John Zapolya.

swap.text: This sultan was surprised by Wallachian troops during the Night Attack at Targoviste [ter-GOH-vish-te], after which Vlad impaled 20,000 Turks. This sultan also invaded Serbia and captured Constantinople.
swap.answerHtml: Mehmed II [accept Mehmed the Conqueror; accept “Mehmet” in place of “Mehmed”]
swap.clue: This ruler established a millet led by Gennadius II, who received authority over all Orthodox Christians in his empire.

question.leadin: The path to becoming one of these people involved "scouting" in the devshirme system.
question.text: Name these boy soldiers from the Balkans who were gathered by the Ottoman empire to fight in the military. They usually specialized in firearms.
question.clue: In a coronation ceremony for a monarch sometimes called "The Sot" or "The Drunkard", this group refused to march to the Topkapi Palace until bribed, and they originally served as a bodyguard for Orkhan.

swap.text: This period of modernization, especially of the millet system, ended when Abdulhamid issued the First Ottoman Constitution.
swap.clue: Soon after the Auspicious Incident, the Ottoman army was modernized during this wider initiative. The introduction of paper money and post offices, as well as units called vilayets, were among the changes introduced during this initiative.

question.leadin: Raphael Lemkin coined a term that was first used to describe this event.
question.text: Name this event that was begun by mass deportations authorized by the Tehcir Law. One country's Article 301 prohibits discussing this event.
question.clue: Discussion of it is suppressed today by Article 301, which has led to the persecution of Hrant Dink and Orhan Pamuk.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the military personnel of Australia.
swap.text: This World War I battle, a disaster planned by Winston Churchill, was fought largely by the ANZAC corps of Australians and New Zealanders. Mustafa Kemal gained fame defending Turkey here.
swap.clue: This World War I battle, also known as the Dardanelles Campaign, that ended in an Ottoman victory over ANZAC forces.

question.text: The Seljuks displaced many people of this ethnicity, who then established a namesake kingdom in Cilicia. These Christians then allowed the First Crusade to pass through their new land.
question.clue: Thanks to Gregory the Illuminator, these people had the world's first official Christian state starting in 301.

swap.leadin: He died at the siege of Szigetvar after resuming warfare in Hungary in 1566.
swap.text: Name this Ottoman sultan, the son of Selim the Grim, who defeated the aforementioned Hungarians at the great battle of Mohacs forty years earlier.
swap.clue: He employed Sinan as the chief architect, married Roxelana, and was often called "kanuni."

question.leadin: Identify these modern cities by their ancient Roman names and histories.
question.text: This city was called Byzantium until Constantine the Great moved his capital there. The modern name of this largest city in Turkey derives from the Turkish pronunciation of "Constantinople."
question.clue: Cannons designed by the Hungarian engineer Orban were used to breach this city's Theodosian Walls.

swap.leadin: (Extra) This group's military wing included Enver Pasha.
swap.text: Name this coalition of groups whose namesake revolution led to the Second Constitutional Era and, later, to the downfall of the Ottoman Empire.
swap.clue: This movement was opposed by a secret society called the Savior Officers.

question.leadin: Though it was long known as the sick man of Europe, the First World War dealt the Ottoman Empire its final blow.
question.text: Give this title held by the three men who were part of the Committee of Union and Progress and de facto led the Ottoman Empire during the war. That triumvirate of men with this title also ordered the Armenian genocide.
question.clue: The genocide was carried out by the Committee of Union and Progress under three de facto leaders with this title. Talaat and Ahmed Cemal ("keh-mal"), who both had this title, were assassinated for their role in the genocide during Operation Nemesis.

swap.leadin: The Polish slave and translator Albertus Bobovius compared this institution to a monastery.
swap.text: Name this institution located in the Topkapı palace whose guards were led by the Chief Black Eunuch. Holders of the title of valide, such as Roxelana, were at the top of this institution's hierarchy.
swap.answerHtml: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire [or the Seraglio]
swap.answer: Imperial Harem of the Ottoman Empire
swap.clue: Talking to members of this institution demystifies it per the letters of Mary Wortley Montagu, which also discussed inoculation.

question.leadin: This initiative resulted in the creation of provincial courts as part of the Vilayet Law, replacing the eyalet system.
question.text: Name this initiative that included the decriminalization of homosexuality and a "reform edict" granting religious freedom to all. This mid-19th century initiative's goals were laid out in the "Supreme Edict of the Rosehouse."
question.clue: The Rescript of the Rose Chamber promised the end of tax farming during this period, during which changes in the millet system attempted to curb nationalism among religious minorities.

swap.text: In 1923, Ataturk's government negotiated this treaty with the Allied forces occupying Turkey. This treaty overturned the Treaty of Sevres ("SEV-ruh"), which would have ceded eastern Thrace and part of the Anatolian coast to Greece.
swap.clue: An earlier treaty signed at the same location was also called the Treaty of Ouchy, and ended the Italo-Turkish War in 1912.

question.leadin: This treaty intended to create a neutral "Zone of Straits" surrounding the Bospohorus and the Dardanelles, and it called for the Malta Tribunals.
question.text: Name this 1920 treaty which proposed divisions of Ottoman lands but was never ratified and replaced with the Treaty of Lausanne.
question.clue: This treaty formalized the territory divisions laid out four months prior at the San Remo Conference, as well the earlier end of hostilities in the Armistice of Mudros.

swap.leadin: This battle took place during a crossing of the Tisza (TEE-zah) River in modern Serbia, where forces under Mustafa II were ambushed, leading to a mutiny by his Janissaries.
swap.text: Name this 1697 victory for a Holy League army under Prince Eugene of Savoy, which forced the Ottomans to agree to the subsequent Treaty of Karlowitz.
swap.clue: At this 1697 battle, Eugene of Savoy led a surprise attack on an Ottoman force attempting to cross the Tisza river. The result was a rout in which the Austrians inflicted over 30,000 casualties on the Ottomans.

question.leadin: Much of this agreement was effectively reversed by the Treaty of Belgrade.
question.text: What 1718 treaty transferred control of the Morea region from the Kingdom of Venice to the Ottomans, but also resulted in the Ottomans surrendering what became the Kingdom of Serbia?

swap.text: The Ottoman forces at Nicopolis were led by this sultan, who later died while imprisoned by Tamerlane.
swap.clue: This man's reign was followed by a twelve year power struggle known as the Interregnum before the confirmation of Mehmet I as sultan.
